title: Engram obligation waiver accepts minted 32-hex record ids
outcome: Engram now mints a record id as a random UUID (32 lowercase hex); ids written earlier are 64 hex. The obligation-waiver path in src/engram_host_adapter.rs validates receipt.resolution, current_definition and expectedDefinition with is_lowercase_sha256 (64 hex only), so it would refuse every obligation created by the new Engram build. Add an Engram record-id check that accepts 32 or 64 lowercase hex and use it at those three sites. is_lowercase_sha256 stays strict: src/review_freeze.rs uses it for the review-freeze fingerprint, which is a real SHA-256. Acceptance: waiver request and response with a 32-hex definition/resolution are accepted; other lengths and non-hex are refused; review-freeze fingerprint validation unchanged; cargo check clean; cargo test --bin termal green.
disposal_reason: Backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 3a re-check, spot-checked by Termal::Fable2): CLOSE-OBSOLETE. No obligation-waiver code remains in src/ on master f7db2c58, so the validator it names is gone.
